story: At 2:17 on a warm, partly cloudy Thursday in Sumter Oaks, Gary and Donna are meeting at the Rec Center, where Gary is stretching his knees and Donna is eager to get their pickleball game started at court one. Hal is out on Magnolia Loop, dutifully counting the pink plastic flamingos in Donna's flock so he can log the number. Meanwhile, Rosa is at home setting out plates and silverware on her dining table and counting chairs so everyone has a seat.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and log the number
Rosa (rosa dining table): Set out plates and silverware, count seats for everyone

gary.thought_process: Hal told me nothing's cleared yet, so the cart stays unmounted until I have approval in writing. I'm at the Rec Center now, and Donna just walked in behind me. She's been pushing me on the paddle lessons and the ladder standings, so the friendly thing is to greet her and let her know I'm ready to practice. Nothing to repeat from earlier, and nothing urgent to file today.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Donna. Knees are stretched and I'm ready to get slaughtered on the court, so go easy on an old HVAC man.

donna.thought_process: We're both finally at the rec center and the courts are right here. I already pitched the lesson and reserved a Tuesday slot, so I shouldn't ask him again. Time to actually get Gary moving: tell him to grab a paddle and start with the basics so he's ready to climb the ladder with me.

parameters.content: Well, here we are, Gary! Grab a paddle and meet me at court one. Rule number one is stay out of the kitchen, and I'll explain that part while we warm up.

hal.thought_process: Gary and Donna have gone to the rec center, so the Loop is empty and I'm standing next to Donna's flamingo flock. My log has to hold up under review, so I'll do a proper count of what's visible from the street right now. I'll keep it factual and fair, since I've promised myself to keep the peace at Rosa's dinner tomorrow. Then I can file it with the committee.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and log the number

rosa.thought_process: It's Thursday afternoon and I've already prepped the beans, pork, and flan, and I checked my shift schedule last tick, so Friday evening is clear. The last unchecked item is the table. I added the centerpiece and made room for Gary's chairs, but I haven't actually confirmed there's a place and enough room for all three neighbors at once. No one is nearby, so I'll use this quiet hour to do a final walkthrough of the dining table and set it, so tomorrow is just cooking and welcoming.

parameters.content: Set out plates and silverware, count seats for everyone

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
